paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is in charge of the whole thing. Gog gets his army, his horses and a crowd of nations, and it all looks like Gog's plan. But God says, "I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out…" (Ezekiel 38:4). Gog thinks he's driving, and he's the one getting TOWED (Ezekiel 38:4, 16).

Why does God do it? He says He will bring Gog "so that the nations may know Me when I show Myself holy in you before their eyes" (Ezekiel 38:16). The chapter ends with the same goal: "Then they will know that I am the LORD" (Ezekiel 38:23). Notice that Israel was living securely, and the danger came anyway (Ezekiel 38:8, 11). So the safety of God's people never depended on walls, because it depends on Him.

So what do you do with that, baker? When the news gets loud and the world looks like it belongs to whoever has the biggest army, you can stay steady. I have sat in a dark drawer thinking nobody was in charge, and I was wrong, so I know that feeling. God said all this ahead of time through the prophets (Ezekiel 38:17), and He still isn't finished with this prophecy. Keep your ovens warm, friend, because there's more to come.
